It's not that celery doesn't have calories - it does - it's that it literally has so few that the energy burned in the digestion of it results in it being a net calorie loss. Plain celery, that is. You still get vitamins and minerals from it, but it is literally useless from a caloric perspective.

Anything colder than body temperature has to be warmed up. Cold water and ice water both qualify, but it's still not as many calories as you think. One calorie is needed to warm one milliliter of water by one degree Celsius. What you see on food labels as a Calorie is actually a kilocalorie. That's the amount needed to raise a liter of water by one degree Celsius. So while you can burn a couple calories that way, it's still not significant in terms of weight loss.

Celery is not a negative calorie food. That's still a myth. It is an extremely low calorie food, but it's still on the positive side according to the Department of Agriculture and the FDA.
